“Because whenever I move my hand away, you find a reason to stand closer.”

Xiaoran opened her mouth, then closed it.

He was right.

She looked away.

“That’s not true.”

“All right.”

“Really.”

“Of course.”

He was smiling again.

She knew that smile.

She didn’t like how easily he could make her feel caught.

Later, when they returned home, Xiaoran went to the bedroom to change.

She came out in comfortable clothes, her hair loosely tied up, and found Yichen standing by the kitchen counter, drinking water.

He looked at her.

“Finished?”

“Yes.”

She walked over and stood in front of him.

He put his glass down.

“What’s wrong?”

“Nothing.”

She wrapped her arms around his waist.

He smiled and rested his hands at her back.

She held him.

Then she pulled away just enough to look at him.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Hold my waist.”

He blinked, then laughed.

“You’re giving me instructions now?”

She nodded.

“Yes.”

He obliged, placing both hands at her waist and drawing her closer.

Xiaoran smiled.

“Like that.”

He looked down at her.

His thumbs moved lightly against her sides.

“Anything else?”

She thought about it, then shook her head.

“No.”

He bent and kissed her hairline.

She looked up.

“Actually...”

“What now?”

“Can you hold me like that when we’re walking too?”

“Of course.”

“And when we’re standing?”

“Yes.”

“And when we’re at home?”

He laughed.

“Xiaoran, I already do.”

She grinned.

“Just checking.”

He shook his head, then leaned down to kiss her.

She kissed him back, her hands resting against his chest.

When they separated, she remained close, looking pleased.

Yichen brushed his thumb along her waist.

“Are you satisfied?”

“Very.”

“Good.”

He kissed her cheek.

Then, just as she started to turn away, he gently drew her back.

“Where are you going?”

“To get water.”

“There’s water here.”

She looked at the glass on the counter.

“Oh.”

His mouth curved.

“Anything else you need?”

She thought, then wrapped her arms around his neck.

“No.”

Yichen laughed and held her, one hand at her waist, exactly where she had told him to put it.

chapters.desc: She shrinks his favorite charcoal shirt, then spends a weekend with conditioner and tutorials trying to rescue it.
chapters.title: The Laundry Incident
chapters.epigraph: “Because it has a story now.”
chapters.content:
The problem began with a shirt.

Not an ordinary shirt, apparently.

It was a dark charcoal-gray button-down, made from a soft fabric, with a relaxed cut and sleeves Yichen usually rolled up to his elbows. Xiaoran had seen him wear it to business meetings, casual dinners, and occasionally around the apartment when he wanted to look presentable without making much effort.

She liked that shirt.

She also liked how Yichen looked in it.

Unfortunately, she had just ruined it.

Or, at least, she thought she had.

It was a Saturday morning. Yichen had gone to the training facility early, leaving Xiaoran with the laundry basket and an ambitious plan to get their apartment properly organized.

She had separated the clothes, checked the labels, and started the washing machine.

Everything had gone smoothly.

Until she took out the charcoal shirt.

She held it up, then frowned, then held it up again.

Something was wrong.

The shirt looked smaller.

Not dramatically smaller, but enough that the shoulders seemed narrower and the sleeves shorter. The fabric had also lost some of its original softness.

Xiaoran checked the washing machine settings, then the care label, then the machine again.

Her expression gradually changed.

“Oh, no.”

She checked the label a second time.

“Oh, no, no, no.”

She had washed it at the wrong temperature.

And she had put it in the dryer.

She stood in the laundry area, holding the shirt in both hands, looking as if she had just received terrible news.

Yichen had other shirts.

Many other shirts.

His wardrobe was larger than hers, and some of his clothes cost more than she wanted to think about. He could replace this shirt without even noticing the expense.

That wasn’t the point.

He liked this one.

She had seen him reach for it repeatedly. She knew it was one of his favorites, even though he had never specifically told her.

And she had ruined it.

Xiaoran looked at the shirt again.

Then she took out her phone.

She searched:

How to fix clothes that shrink after washing.

The results weren’t encouraging.

She tried another search.

Can you restore a shirt after accidentally putting it in the dryer?

Then another.

How to stretch cotton blend fabric.

She stared at the screen.

“Please work.”

Yichen came home shortly after noon.

He found Xiaoran in the bedroom, sitting cross-legged on the floor beside an open laundry basket.

There were several of his shirts folded neatly beside her.

She looked up when he entered.

“You’re back!”

“Mm. What are you doing?” He put his gym bag down.

“Nothing.”

He looked at the clothes.

“Nothing?”

“Organizing.”

His gaze moved to her face.

She was smiling.

A little too brightly.

“Everything all right?”

“Of course.”

He pressed a kiss to her hair.

“Did you eat?”

“Yes.”

“What?”

“Food.”

He met her eyes.

She smiled.

“Rice. Chicken. Vegetables. A very balanced meal.”

“Good.”

He changed out of his training clothes, showered, and returned to the bedroom.

Xiaoran had already gathered the remaining laundry.

He noticed the charcoal shirt folded separately on the far end of the bed.

“Is that mine?”

She froze.

“Yes.”

“Why is it over there?”

“Because...”

She looked at the shirt, then at him, then back at the shirt.

“I made a mistake.”

Yichen’s expression changed slightly.

“What happened?”

She picked up the shirt and held it out.

“I washed it.”

He looked at it, then at her.

“All right.”

“I used the wrong temperature.”

He examined the fabric, running his fingers over the material.

“And?”

“I put it in the dryer.”

He looked at the shirt again.

Then he understood.

“It shrank?”

Xiaoran nodded.

Her mouth pressed into a small line.

“I think so.”

Yichen held it up against himself, examining the shoulders.

“It did.”

Her expression fell.

“I’m sorry.”

He turned to her.

“Xiaoran.”

“I checked the label. I really did. I thought it was okay because the other shirts were fine, but I must have missed the temperature instructions, and then I put everything in the dryer because I thought it would be faster.”

He listened.

“I tried searching for ways to fix it, but I’m not sure if any of them work. I haven’t done anything else to it because I didn’t want to make it worse.”

She took a breath.

“I’m sorry. I know you like this shirt.”

Yichen looked at her.

Then he placed the shirt on the bed.

He opened his arms.

She hesitated.

“Why?”

“Come here first.”

She stepped closer.

He put his hands around her waist.

“Are you upset?”

“Of course I’m upset. I ruined your shirt.”

“That’s not what I asked.”

She blinked.

Yichen brushed his thumb over her side.

“Have you been worrying about this all morning?”

She hesitated.

“...A little.”

“How little?”

She looked away.

That got a smile out of him.

“Xiaoran.”

“Quite a lot.”

He let out a quiet breath, then kissed her hair.

“It’s a shirt.”

“I know.”

“I can buy another one.”

“I know.”

“I can buy ten.”

She gave him a small, unwilling smile.

“That’s not helping.”

“Why?”

“Because I know you can buy another one. But it won’t be the same shirt.”

Yichen looked at her.

That, he understood.

It wasn’t about the money. It wasn’t about replacing something expensive.

She knew he could afford to replace it. She was upset because she had damaged something he liked, something she had wanted to take care of.

He gently lifted her chin.

“Look at me.”

She did.

“I’m not angry.”

Her expression softened a little.

He kissed her cheek.

“And I’m more concerned that you’ve been sitting here looking miserable over a shirt.”

She let out a small laugh.

“I don’t look miserable.”

“You do.”

“You’re exaggerating.”

“Your eyebrows have been doing this all morning.”

He lightly touched the space between her brows.

She immediately frowned again.

He smiled.

“That.”

She pushed his hand away.

“Stop.”

He caught her hand and kissed her knuckles.

“Don’t worry about it anymore.”

“But—”

“We’ll see if it can be fixed. If it can’t, I’ll keep it or replace it. That’s all.”

She met his eyes.

“You’re really not upset?”

“Xiaoran, I own more shirts than I can reasonably wear.”

She laughed.

“That’s true.”

“And I have a girlfriend who apparently takes laundry very seriously.”

She gave him a look.

“Don’t make fun of me.”

“I’m not.”

He kissed her, briefly again.

“Come on. Let’s have lunch.”

Yichen thought the matter was settled.

Xiaoran, however, had other plans.

For the rest of that day and the next, he noticed several unusual things.

First, the charcoal shirt had disappeared from the bedroom.

Second, Xiaoran became strangely protective of the laundry area.

Third, whenever he entered the room while she was holding her phone, she would immediately switch applications.

He noticed.

He didn’t say anything.

On Sunday afternoon, he came home from a short training session and found the bedroom door slightly open.

Xiaoran was sitting at the dressing table.

In front of her was the charcoal shirt.

There was also a bowl of water, a towel, a bottle of hair conditioner, and her laptop.

Yichen stopped at the doorway.

He watched her carefully stretch one sleeve.

She leaned closer to examine the fabric.

Then she consulted something on her laptop.

Then she stretched it again.

Yichen stood there for several seconds.

Finally, he spoke.

“What’s happening?”

Xiaoran startled.

The sleeve slipped from her hands.

She turned around.

“Yichen!”

He looked at the arrangement on the desk, then at her.

“Is this a science experiment?”

She immediately reached for the towel.

“No.”

He walked closer.

“Then what are you doing?”

“Nothing.”

He looked at the shirt.

“You’re trying to fix it.”

She didn’t answer.

He glanced at the laptop.

The search page was still open.

How to safely stretch a shrunken shirt without damaging the fabric.

Below it were several tabs.

One was a video tutorial.

Another was an article about fabric composition.

A third was a discussion forum.

Yichen looked back at her.

“Xiaoran.”

She lowered her eyes.

“I was just trying something.”

He sat down on the end of the bed beside her.

“For how long?”

She shrugged.

“Not long.”

He looked at the open tabs.

“How long?”

She hesitated.

“Since yesterday.”

“Yesterday?”

She nodded.

“I thought maybe I could restore some of the original shape.”

He looked at the shirt.

“Did it work?”

She made a small face.

“Not really.”

Yichen pressed his lips together, trying not to smile.

She noticed.

“Don’t laugh.”

“I’m not.”

“You’re smiling.”

“I’m looking at you.”

“You’re smiling while looking at me.”

He finally laughed.

Not loudly, but enough that she became increasingly embarrassed.

“Yichen!”

He reached for her hand.

“Why didn’t you tell me?”

She looked down.

“Because you already said it was fine.”

“And?”

“I thought I could fix it.”

He watched her.

Then he glanced at the shirt again.

“Did you spend all yesterday researching this?”

“Not all day.”

“Xiaoran.”

“...A few hours.”

He leaned back slightly.

“How many?”

She held up two fingers.

“Two?”

She hesitated.

“Maybe three.”

He laughed again.

She immediately looked offended.

“It’s not funny!”

He reached over and pulled her gently toward him.

“All right. I’m sorry.”

She settled sideways on his lap, still looking a little embarrassed.

He rested one hand at her waist.

“Listen to me.”

She turned to him.

“You don’t have to repair everything you accidentally damage.”

She lowered her gaze.

“I know.”

“And you certainly don’t have to spend your weekend trying to restore a shirt.”

She was quiet.

Yichen brushed a strand of hair behind her ear.

“I know you wanted to fix it because you felt bad. But I would rather have you spend those three hours doing something you enjoy.”

“Like what?”

“Watching your dramas. Eating snacks. Annoying me.”

She laughed despite herself.

“I don’t annoy you.”

“You do.”

“You’re terrible.”

He laughed under his breath.

“Fortunately, I like you.”

She rested her forehead against his shoulder.

“I just wanted to do something nice for you.”

His expression softened.

He placed a kiss against her hair.

“You already do.”

A little later, Yichen examined the shirt again.

The fabric had recovered some of its shape, though it wasn’t quite the same. The sleeves were still slightly shorter, and the material remained a little different from its original texture.

He held it up.

Xiaoran stood beside him, watching anxiously.

“Is it okay?”

Yichen looked at the shirt.

Then he put it on.

The fit was a little snug around the shoulders, but still wearable.

He rolled the sleeves up.

Xiaoran studied him.

“Does it feel uncomfortable?”

“No.”

She stepped closer and adjusted the collar.

“It looks different.”

“Does it?”

“A little.”

He held her gaze.

“Do you dislike it?”

She shook her head.

“No. It still looks good.”

“Then I’ll keep it.”

She blinked.

“You’re going to wear it?”

“Why not?”

“But it’s smaller.”

“I noticed.”

“Yichen.”

He studied her.

“I like this shirt. I can still wear it. And if it eventually becomes uncomfortable, I’ll stop wearing it.”

She looked at him.

Then she smiled.

“Okay.”

He turned slightly.

“How do I look?”

She examined him with exaggerated seriousness.

“Very handsome.”

“Good.”

“Although...”

“Although?”

She reached out and rolled one sleeve a little higher.

“Now you look even better.”

He caught her wrist and kissed the inside of it.

“Your assessment is appreciated.”

She laughed.

That evening, Xiaoran was sitting on the sofa, watching a drama while Yichen worked on his laptop.

He was still wearing the charcoal shirt.

She noticed it several times.

Eventually, she paused the episode.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Can I ask you something?”

He looked up.

“Of course.”

“Was that really one of your favorite shirts?”

He considered the question.

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Comfortable. Good fabric. Easy to wear.”

She looked down at her hands.

“Did you buy it a long time ago?”

“About two years ago.”

“Oh.”

He watched her.

“Why?”

She shrugged.

“I just wanted to know.”

He closed his laptop.

“Xiaoran.”

“Do you think I liked the shirt more than I like having you around?”

Her eyes widened.

“No!”

“Then why are you still thinking about it?”

She laughed awkwardly.

“I don’t know.”

He moved closer.

He reached for her.

She shifted toward him.

He placed an arm around her waist and drew her against his chest.

“Besides, I think it has become a rather interesting shirt,” he said.

“Why?”

“Because it has a story now.”

She looked up.

“A story?”

He nodded.

“My girlfriend accidentally shrank it, spent three hours trying to rescue it, and then nearly conducted a scientific experiment in our bedroom.”

Xiaoran covered her face.

“Please don’t tell anyone.”

He laughed.

“I won’t.”

“Especially Fang Ze.”

“Him least of all.”

She relaxed.

Then she looked at him again.

“Can I still do the laundry?”

He blinked.

“Why wouldn’t you?”

“Because maybe you don’t trust me anymore.”

Yichen looked at her.

Then his expression softened.

“Xiaoran, I’m not going to ban you from doing laundry because one shirt shrank.”

That made her grin.

“Okay.”

“We’ll just pay more attention to the labels.”

She nodded.

“And maybe I shouldn’t put everything in the dryer.”

“That would be a good start.”

She leaned closer and kissed his cheek.

“Thank you for not being angry.”

He turned his face and kissed her lips.

“Thank you for caring.”

She smiled against his mouth.

A week later, Xiaoran opened the wardrobe and found something unexpected.

The charcoal shirt was hanging in its usual place.

Beside it was a new shirt.

Almost identical.

Same charcoal-gray color, similar cut, similar fabric.

She took it off the hanger and examined it.

Then she turned toward Yichen, who was buttoning his watch.

“Did you buy another one?”

He glanced over.

“Yes.”

She looked at the shirt again.

“Why?”

“The old one is a little small.”

“But you said you could still wear it.”

“I can.”

“Then why buy another?”

He finished adjusting his watch.

“Because I liked it.”

She frowned slightly.

“Yichen.”

“What?”

“You really don’t need to replace everything.”

“I know.”

“Then?”

He walked over and took the shirt from her hands, hanging it back in the wardrobe.

“Because I wanted another one.”

She held his gaze.

He kissed her.

“The old one stays. The new one is for when I want the original fit.”

She nodded slowly.

Then she looked at the two shirts side by side.

One new.

One slightly imperfect.

She reached out and touched the older shirt.

“Are you sure you don’t mind?”

Yichen followed her gaze.

Then he put his arm around her waist.

“Not even a little.”

She turned toward him.

Her expression softened.

He kissed her cheek.

“And for the record, I don’t need you to take care of my belongings perfectly.”

“I know.”

“I just need you to stop looking so sad whenever something goes wrong.”

She laughed.

“I’ll try.”

He gave her waist a gentle squeeze.

“Good.”

“Although, if you’re planning to conduct another experiment, perhaps use one of Fang Ze’s shirts,” he said, with a smile.

Xiaoran burst out laughing.

“Yichen!”

“What? He has plenty.”

“You’re so mean.”

He smiled and kissed her cheek again.

The old charcoal shirt stayed in the wardrobe, and Yichen still wore it sometimes.

And every time he did, Xiaoran would look at him with a little smile.

He never told her that he sometimes chose it deliberately.

He liked seeing that smile.

chapters.desc: She has forty minutes to get ready for dinner with her friends. He has just come home, and he is in no hurry to let her finish.
chapters.title: An Unexpected Back Hug
chapters.epigraph: “Because you’re here.”
chapters.content:
Xiaoran was halfway through doing her makeup when Yichen came home.

She heard the front door open, followed by the familiar sound of his keys dropping into the bowl by the door.

“I’m home.”

She looked at herself in the mirror.

“Welcome back!”

Yichen walked into the bedroom a moment later, still wearing his training clothes. His hair was slightly damp from his shower at the facility, and he had a sports bag hanging from one shoulder.

He stopped at the doorway.

Xiaoran was sitting in front of the dressing table, wearing a pale pink top and a skirt. Her makeup products were arranged across the tabletop, and she was carefully applying mascara with one hand while holding her phone in the other.

He watched her for a few seconds.

“Going out?”

“Mm-hm.”

“With your team?”

“No, with Jiayi and Ning. We’re having dinner.”

He put his bag down.

“What time?”

“Seven.”

Yichen glanced at the clock.

It was 6:18.

“You’re almost ready?”

“Almost.”

He looked at the number of products spread across the table, then at her face.

“How long have you been getting ready? Not long.”

“How long?”

“Twenty minutes.”

Something in his face eased.

She immediately narrowed her eyes at his reflection.

“You’re looking at me like you don’t believe me.”

“I didn’t say anything.”

“You don’t have to.”

He laughed and walked toward the bathroom to wash his hands.

Xiaoran returned to her mascara.

She had absolutely no idea that the next twenty minutes would become more difficult.

Yichen returned wearing a clean dark T-shirt and comfortable trousers.

He walked behind her chair, glanced at her reflection, and placed one hand lightly on her shoulder.

“Hello.”

She smiled at him through the mirror.

“Hello.”

He bent down and kissed her temple.

“How was your day?”

“Good. Busy, though.”

“What happened?”

She began telling him about a project at work, explaining how one of her colleagues had changed the direction of a presentation at the last minute.

Yichen listened, occasionally asking questions.

His hand moved from her shoulder to her upper arm.

Then, as she continued speaking, he walked around the chair and stood beside her.

She was reaching for her blush when he leaned down and kissed her cheek.

Xiaoran smiled.

“You’re interrupting.”

“Sorry.”

He didn’t sound sorry.

She dipped her brush into the blush.

“Anyway, as I was saying—”

He kissed her other cheek.

She stopped.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“I’m talking.”

“I know.”

“Then listen.”

“I’m listening.”

She looked at him through the mirror.

He was smiling.

She pointed her brush at him.

“Don’t look at me like that.”

“Like what?”

“That.”

His smile grew.

“All right.”

He walked away.

Xiaoran watched him disappear into the living area, then shook her head with a smile.

Finally.

Peace.

She returned to her makeup.

Five minutes later, she was carefully blending eyeshadow when she felt a pair of arms slide around her waist from behind.

She startled slightly.

“Ah!”

Yichen rested his chin on her shoulder.

“Sorry.”

She looked at him in the mirror.

“You scared me!”

He laughed under his breath.

“You were concentrating.”

“Obviously. I’m doing my makeup.”

He hummed.

His hands settled comfortably against her waist, fingers resting just above her hips.

Xiaoran tried to continue blending her eyeshadow.

It was difficult. He wasn’t doing anything disruptive. He was there.

Warm, close, and entirely too comfortable.

She glanced at his reflection.

“Why are you standing like this?”

“Can I not?”

“You can. But I’m doing something.”

“I noticed.”

He kissed the side of her neck, just below her ear.

Her brush stopped.

Yichen smiled against her skin.

“Continue.”

She turned her head slightly.

“How?”

He laughed.

“Your makeup.”

“You’re the reason I can’t continue.”

He looked at her reflection.

“Would you like me to move?”

Xiaoran considered it.

Then, rather than answer, she leaned back against him.

Yichen’s smile softened.

He tightened his arms slightly around her waist.

Neither spoke.

Then she lifted her brush again.

“Okay. Now don’t move.”

“All right.”

He lasted about forty seconds.

Xiaoran was applying blush to her other cheek when his fingers began tracing small, absentminded circles against her waist.

She glanced down.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Your hand.”

He stopped.

“What’s wrong?”

“You’re tickling me.”

“Sorry.”

She continued.

His hand remained still.

She was almost finished blending when he leaned forward and kissed her cheek again.

She closed her eyes.

“Zhou Yichen.”

He laughed.

“Yes?”

“Are you bored?”

“No.”

“Then why are you bothering me?”

He looked at her reflection.

“Because you’re here.”

She blinked.

That was unfair.

He knew exactly how to say things like that without making a big deal out of them.

She tried to hide her smile.

“That’s not a proper answer.”

“It’s an honest one.”

She met his eyes, then turned her attention back to the mirror.

“Fine. But I need to finish.”

“Go ahead.”

He kissed her temple.

“Take your time.”

Xiaoran moved on to her eyeliner.

This was the most delicate part of her makeup, and she needed both concentration and a steady hand.

Yichen seemed to understand this.

For the first time since coming home, he became quiet.

His arms remained around her waist, but he didn’t move.

Xiaoran was grateful.

She carefully drew the first line, then the second.

She leaned back slightly to inspect the result.

“Good.”

Yichen looked at her reflection.

“Looks nice.”

“Thank you.”

She was about to reach for her eyeliner again when he spoke.

“Can I ask you something?”

“Yes.”

“Why are you wearing earrings?”

She turned to him.

“Because they’re pretty.”

He glanced at the small flower-shaped earrings.

“The ones you bought?”

She nodded.

“Yes.”

“They suit you.”

She grinned.

“I know.”

He laughed.

She reached for her lipstick.

Then felt him press a kiss against her shoulder.

She stopped.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“You’re doing it again.”

“What am I doing?”

“Being affectionate.”

He raised his eyebrows.

“Is that a problem?”

She looked at him in the mirror.

“Not normally.”

“Then?”

She held up the lipstick.

“Do you see this?”

He looked at it.

“Yes.”

“I’m trying to apply it.”

“Understood.”

She waited.

He didn’t move.

She turned her head slightly.

“You’re not going to kiss me while I’m wearing lipstick.”

“Why not?”

“Because you’ll ruin it.”

“Then I’ll wait.”

She looked satisfied.

“Good.”

He lowered his head and kissed her bare cheek instead.

Xiaoran stared at him.

“That doesn’t count.”

He laughed.

By 6:42, Xiaoran was finally applying lipstick.

Yichen had moved to stand behind her again, his arms loosely around her waist.

She carefully applied the color, pressed her lips together, then reached for a tissue.

“Almost done.”

Yichen looked at her reflection.

“Pretty.”

Her mouth tipped up.

“Thank you.”

She leaned toward the mirror to check the corners.

He watched her.

Then, gently, he turned her chair a few degrees toward him.

Xiaoran looked up.

“What?”

He bent slightly.

She immediately raised one finger.

“No.”

He paused.

She pointed at her lips.

“Just finished.”

He looked at her, then smiled.

“All right.”

“Good.”

He bent and kissed her hairline.

Then her cheek, then the tip of her nose.

Xiaoran laughed.

“You’re ridiculous.”

He straightened.

She turned back toward the mirror, then looked at her reflection.

Her lipstick was intact.

She couldn’t help smiling.

“See? You can behave.”

Yichen rested his chin on her shoulder.

“For how long?”

She held his gaze.

“At least until I finish.”

“Understood.”

The final step was perfume.

Xiaoran reached for the bottle she had chosen and sprayed a little onto her wrists.

Then she turned her head toward Yichen.

“How does it smell?”

He leaned closer to her wrist.

“Nice.”

She smiled.

“Do you like it?”

“Yes.”

She offered the other wrist.

He took her hand and brought it closer, smelling the fragrance.

Then he kissed the inside of her wrist.

Xiaoran looked down at him.

“That’s not how you’re supposed to test perfume.”

Something in his face eased.

“Isn’t it?”

“No.”

He kissed her wrist again.

She laughed.

“Yichen!”

He released her hand.

“All right.”

She put the bottle away and looked at herself one last time.

Her makeup was finished. Her hair was neat.

Her earrings were in place.

She was finally ready.

She stood up.

Yichen’s arms naturally came around her waist again.

She tilted her head.

“Finished.”

He glanced at her face, then at her outfit.

“Beautiful.”

“Thank you.”

He brushed his thumb along her waist.

He crooked a finger at her.

She tilted her head.

“Why?”

He leaned down.

“Now I can kiss you.”

She laughed.

“You’ve been kissing me this whole time!”

“Not properly.”

Before she could answer, he kissed her.

She wrapped her arms around his shoulders, careful at first because of her lipstick, but he was gentle. His hand rested against her back while the other stayed at her waist.

When he pulled away, he looked at her lips.

“Still intact.”

That made her grin.

“Of course.”

He kissed her once more, this time just at the corner of her mouth.

A few minutes later, Xiaoran was standing near the entrance, checking her handbag.

Yichen came to see her off.

She glanced at him.

“You’re not coming with me, right?”

“No. I have something to review.”

She nodded.

“Okay.”

He walked toward her.

“Have fun.”

“I will.”

He adjusted the strap of her bag where it had twisted against her shoulder.

“Text me when you arrive.”

“I will.”

“And when you’re leaving.”

She laughed.

“Yes, Zhou Yichen.”

He smiled and kissed her hair.

She was about to open the door when he caught her hand.

“Wait.”

She turned.

“What?”

He met her eyes.

Then gently pulled her back toward him, wrapping his arms around her waist.

Xiaoran looked up.

“Another one?”

“One more.”

She laughed.

“You’re very clingy today.”

He lowered his head.

He kissed her cheek.

Then her forehead.

Then, after a brief pause, he smiled.

“Have I ruined your makeup?”

She examined his face.

“No.”

“Good.”

She reached up and adjusted the collar of his shirt.

“Although you’ve made me late.”

He glanced at the clock.

“By three minutes.”

“Three important minutes.”

He laughed.

“Sorry.”

She kissed his cheek.

“Forgiven.”

Then she finally left.

At 8:16, Yichen received a photograph.

It was a selfie of Xiaoran at the restaurant, sitting between Jiayi and Ning.

Her makeup still looked perfect.

Xiaoran: Look! My makeup survived.

He smiled.

Yichen: Impressive.

Xiaoran: You didn’t ruin it.

Yichen: You’re welcome.

Xiaoran: Don’t be so proud. I did all the work.

Yichen: I provided moral support.

She sent him a laughing sticker.

A few seconds later, another message arrived.

Xiaoran: Actually, I miss you.

Yichen looked at the message, then replied.

Yichen: Enjoy dinner. I’ll be here when you get back.

She sent a heart.

He put his phone down and returned to his tablet.

When Xiaoran returned home that night, it was nearly eleven.

She opened the door, expecting Yichen to have gone to bed.

Instead, she found him sitting on the sofa with his laptop open.

He looked up.

“Back?”

That made her grin.

“Mm-hm.”

“Had fun?”

“Very much.”

He closed his laptop and stood.

She walked toward him, immediately slipping her arms around his waist.

Yichen looked down.

“What’s this?”

“A hug.”

“I can see that.”

She rested her cheek against his chest, then looked up.

“Did you miss me?”

He brushed her hair away from her face.

“The apartment was too quiet.”

She laughed.

“Poor you.”

“Very.”

He kissed her, briefly.

She pulled away slightly and pointed at her face.

“Look.”

He examined her.

“What?”

“My makeup is still perfect.”

That got a smile out of him.

“Congratulations.”

She narrowed her eyes.

“You’re not impressed?”

“I am.”

She smiled proudly.

“See? I can go out, have fun, and come home with everything intact.”

Yichen nodded.

“Very capable.”

She leaned closer.

“Although...”

“Hm?”

“I think I might need to redo my lipstick.”

He turned to her.

“Why?”

She smiled mischievously.

“Because someone kept trying to kiss me earlier.”

Yichen’s mouth curved into that slow, knowing smile.

“Is that so?”

She nodded.

He stepped closer, his hands finding her waist as naturally as ever.

“Then perhaps I should make it worth reapplying.”

Xiaoran’s cheeks warmed.

“Yichen.”

He laughed and kissed her.

This time, she didn’t have to worry about finishing her makeup.

And when they finally separated, she looked up at him with a smile.

“You’re terrible.”

He brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“Yet you keep coming back.”

She laughed and hugged him again.

“Unfortunately.”

Yichen kissed her hair.

He knew perfectly well she didn’t mean it.

chapters.desc: A balcony door that locks itself, eleven floors up, and the friend who has had their spare key since moving day.
chapters.title: The Spare Key Incident
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t save you. Fang Ze did.”
chapters.content:
The first mistake was leaving the balcony door open. The second was closing it.

The third, and arguably the most significant, was assuming Zhou Yichen would remember where he had put the spare key.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

Xiaoran stood in the middle of the balcony, holding two mugs of tea.

“Did you lock the door?”

He looked up from his phone.

There was a brief silence.

Then he glanced at the glass door behind her.

Xiaoran followed his gaze.

The handle was down.

The door was shut.

She tried it.

Once.

Twice.

Then she turned slowly.

“Yichen.”

He stood up.

“Wait.”

She tried the handle again, as if the result might change if she approached it with a more optimistic attitude.

It didn’t.

The balcony door had automatically locked behind them.

And they were outside.

For a few seconds, neither spoke.

The balcony was comfortable enough. It was a mild evening, the city lights were beginning to come on, and there were two chairs, a small table, and a potted plant Xiaoran had been trying to keep alive for three months.

It was also eleven floors up.

And the only way back inside was through the locked glass door.

Xiaoran looked at Yichen.

He looked at the door, then at her.

“Do you have your phone?”

She held it up.

“Yes.”

“Good.”

He took his own phone from his pocket.

Xiaoran stared at him.

“Why are you so calm?”

“Because we’re not in danger.”

“We’re locked out.”

“On our balcony.”

“That’s still locked out.”

He smiled.

“All right.”

She put the mugs down on the table.

“Can you open it?”

He tried the handle.

It didn’t move.

He checked the lock.

Nothing.

Then he looked at the door frame, examining it as if he might find a practical solution through sheer concentration.

Xiaoran watched him.

“Can you break it?”

“No.”

“Why?”

“Because it’s our door.”

“That’s a very good point.”

He met her eyes.

“Thank you.”

She folded her arms.

“What’s the plan?”

Yichen unlocked his phone.

“Call Fang Ze.”

Xiaoran blinked.

“Why Fang Ze?”

“He has our spare key.”

She blinked at him, then at the door, then back at him.

“Why does Fang Ze have our spare key?”

“Because he lives nearby.”

It wasn’t an answer, and they both knew it.

“On moving day. In case.”

Xiaoran narrowed her eyes.

“You gave Fang Ze a key to our home?”

“Yes.”

“Without telling me?”

“I told you.”

“When?”

“On moving day. When I gave it to him.”

She opened her mouth.

Closed it.

Thought.

Then she pointed at him.

“I was carrying a box.”

“Yes.”

“I was very busy.”

“I noticed.”

“You should have reminded me.”

That got a smile out of him.

“All right. I’ll remind you next time.”

She looked deeply unimpressed.

Fang Ze answered on the third ring.

“Captain?”

He still called him that, from university, although on the Herons neither of them was captain of anything.

“Are you home?”

“Yes. What’s up?”

“Do you still have our spare key?”

There was a pause.

Then Fang Ze said, “Why?”

Yichen glanced at Xiaoran.

“We’re locked out.”

Another pause.

Then—

“Where?”

“On the balcony.”

Silence.

Yichen waited.

Fang Ze made a sound.

It wasn’t quite a laugh.

“You’re joking.”

“I’m not.”

“How?”

Xiaoran leaned toward the phone.

“Don’t ask how. Just come and save us.”

Fang Ze started laughing.

Yichen looked at her.

She mouthed, Tell him to hurry.

Yichen sighed.

“Can you come over?”

“Of course. Give me fifteen minutes.”

“Thank you.”

“Wait.”

Yichen paused.

“What?”

“Are you both actually outside?”

“Yes.”

“On the balcony?”

“Yes, Fang Ze.”

Fang Ze burst out laughing.

Xiaoran closed her eyes.

“Fang Ze.”

“Sorry. Sorry. I’m coming.”

The call ended.

Yichen put his phone away.

Xiaoran stared at him.

“Fifteen minutes?”

“That’s what he said.”

She looked at the city, then at the door, then at the two mugs of tea.

“Well.”

Yichen pulled out one of the chairs.

“Sit down.”

She met his eyes.

“You’re treating this like a picnic.”

“We have tea.”

“We’re locked outside our own home.”

“We also have tea.”

She stared at him for another moment.

Then she sat down.

Five minutes later, Xiaoran was regretting several decisions.

The first wasn’t bringing her cardigan. The second was agreeing to sit outside.

The third was having a boyfriend who seemed perfectly content to treat an accidental balcony confinement as a minor scheduling inconvenience.

Yichen noticed her rubbing her arms.

“Cold?”

“A little.”

He stood and took off his jacket.

She accepted it.

“Thank you.”

He sat down beside her.

For a while, they watched the traffic below.

Then Xiaoran turned toward him.

“Do you think Fang Ze will tell the team?”

Yichen looked at her.

“Probably.”

“Yichen.”

“He’ll tell Kou Ran.”

“Then Kou Ran will tell everyone.”

“Probably.”

She groaned.

“We’re never going to hear the end of this.”

Yichen smiled.

“Maybe not.”

She leaned against his shoulder.

“You’re not worried?”

“About Fang Ze telling them?”

“Yes.”

“No.”

“Why?”

“Because it’s funny.”

She lifted her head.

“You’re enjoying this.”

He didn’t deny it. She gave him an offended look.

He reached over and tucked the jacket more securely around her shoulders.

“At least we’re together.”

Xiaoran looked at him.

“That’s a very romantic way to describe being trapped.”

“Would you prefer I said I regret being here?”

She considered it.

“No.”

“Then we’re fine.”

She leaned against him again.

At the twelve-minute mark, Fang Ze sent a message.

Fang Ze: On my way.

Fang Ze: Stopped downstairs to buy something.

Fang Ze: Do you want anything?

Xiaoran immediately reached for her phone.

Xiaoran: Warm milk tea.

Yichen glanced at her.

“You’re ordering drinks?”

“We’re waiting.”

“We have tea.”

“It’s cold.”

He looked at the mugs, then at her.

“All right.”

She sent another message.

Xiaoran: Half sugar. No pearls.

Xiaoran: Thank you, savior.

Fang Ze replied almost immediately.

Fang Ze: You’re welcome.

Fang Ze: Please don’t lock yourselves out again.

Xiaoran showed Yichen the message.

He smiled.

“He’s very concerned.”

“He should be.”

A few seconds later, Fang Ze sent another message.

Fang Ze: Actually, should I take a photo when I arrive?

Xiaoran sat up.

“No.”

Yichen took the phone from her hand.

“Don’t encourage him.”

He typed a reply.

Yichen: Just bring the key.

Fang Ze reacted with a laughing emoji.

Xiaoran sighed.

“He’s going to be unbearable.”

Yichen handed her phone back.

“He’s already unbearable.”

At twenty minutes, Fang Ze finally arrived.

They heard the flat doorbell from outside.

Xiaoran sat upright.

“That’s him!”

Yichen stood.

“Stay there.”

She gave him a look.

“Where am I going to go?”

He walked to the glass door and knocked twice.

Inside, the flat door opened.

Fang Ze’s voice carried through the hallway.

“Captain?”

Yichen called back, “Balcony.”

There was a pause.

Then Fang Ze appeared in the living room, carrying a plastic bag.

He stopped.

Looked at Yichen.

Then at Xiaoran, who was sitting on the balcony chair with Yichen’s jacket around her shoulders, then at the locked door.

He stared for a second.

And started laughing.

Xiaoran pointed at him.

“Don’t.”

Fang Ze tried to compose himself.

He failed.

“I’m sorry.”

“No, you’re not.”

“You’re right.”

Yichen held out his hand.

“The key.”

Fang Ze walked over, still grinning.

He unlocked the door.

The sound of the latch clicking open was the most beautiful sound Xiaoran had heard all evening.

She immediately stepped inside.

“Thank you.”

Fang Ze bowed slightly.

“You’re welcome.”

Then he looked at Yichen.

“Captain, I didn’t know you were capable of such a thing.”

Yichen stepped inside.

“Such a thing?”

“Getting locked out of your own home.”

“It was an accident.”

“With Xiaoran?”

Xiaoran turned.

“Why are you saying it like that?”

Fang Ze lifted both hands.

“Nothing. Nothing.”

Yichen closed the balcony door behind them.

Then he took the plastic bag from Fang Ze.

“What’s this?”

“Your milk tea.”

Xiaoran brightened.

“You actually bought it!”

“Of course. I was already downstairs.”

She accepted the drink.

“Thank you, Fang Ze.”

His mouth curved.

“You’re welcome. Although I think I deserve more than a thank-you.”

Yichen looked at him.

“What do you want?”

Fang Ze considered it.

“Food.”

“All right.”

“And maybe a photo.”

“No.”

Fang Ze laughed.

“Come on. Just one.”

Xiaoran immediately stepped behind Yichen.

“No photos.”

Fang Ze looked between them.

“You’re both very protective of your dignity.”

Yichen took the spare key from him.

“Thank you for coming.”

Fang Ze nodded, still smiling.

Then he looked at Xiaoran.

“Next time, please make sure you have your phone.”

She lifted her milk tea.

“I did.”

“Good. And maybe don’t lock the door.”

“That was not intentional!”

“I know.”

He walked toward the entrance, then stopped.

Turned back.

“Actually, one more thing.”

Yichen looked at him.

“What?”

Fang Ze pointed at the balcony.

“Do you want me to leave the key with you, or should I keep it?”

Yichen glanced at Xiaoran.

A long silence followed.

Then Xiaoran said, carefully, “Maybe you should keep it.”

Fang Ze nodded.

“Wise decision.”

The incident should have ended there.

It didn’t.

Because Fang Ze had friends.

And those friends had phones.

By the next morning, the team group chat had become unbearable.

Kou Ran: Heard the captain had a difficult evening.

Fang Ze: Very difficult.

Kou Ran: Everything okay?

Fang Ze: He survived.

Fang Ze: Xiaoran too.

Fang Ze: I saved them.

Kou Ran: From what?

Fang Ze: Their own balcony.

There was a pause, then the group chat exploded.

Qin Lei: WHAT?

Bao Dong: HOW?

Kou Ran: Zhou, please explain.

Fang Ze: No explanation necessary. I witnessed it myself.

Kou Ran: Were they both outside?

Fang Ze: Yes.

Kou Ran: Together?

Fang Ze: Yes.

Kou Ran: On their own balcony?

Fang Ze: YES.

Xiaoran was sitting at the dining table, eating breakfast, when Yichen’s phone began vibrating repeatedly.

She looked up.

“What’s happening?”

He glanced at the screen.

“Nothing.”

“Yichen.”

He turned the phone over.

“Fang Ze.”

She sighed.

“Of course.”

Yichen took a sip of coffee.

Then his phone vibrated again.

He checked it.

This time, he actually smiled.

Xiaoran put down her fork.

“What?”

He turned the screen toward her.

A message from Kou Ran.

Kou Ran: Zhou, next time you want some fresh air, just open a window.

Xiaoran stared.

Then she buried her face in her hands.

“I’m going to kill Fang Ze.”

Yichen laughed.

Later that afternoon, she found Yichen checking the balcony door.

He tested the handle.

Opened it.

Closed it.

Opened it again.

Xiaoran stood behind him.

“What are you doing?”

“Checking the lock.”

“Why?”

“To make sure it works.”

She folded her arms.

“It worked perfectly. We were the problem.”

“That’s true.”

He opened the door again, then checked the locking mechanism.

After a moment, he nodded.

“Fine.”

Xiaoran stepped onto the balcony.

Then she turned around.

“Actually, I think we should put a spare key somewhere.”

He turned to her.

“We have one.”

“Not outside.”

He considered that.

“Where?”

She looked at the small table, then the potted plant, then the balcony railing.

Yichen followed her gaze.

“No.”

She blinked.

“What?”

“Don’t hide a key under the plant.”

“I wasn’t going to.”

He raised an eyebrow.

She hesitated.

“Not necessarily.”

He laughed.

Then he reached into his pocket and held out a small key.

Xiaoran looked at it.

“What’s that?”

“A spare.”

She looked at him.

“You had another one?”

“Yes.”

“Since when?”

“Since we moved in.”

She took it from his hand.

“Why didn’t you tell me?”

“I thought you knew.”

She turned to him.

Then she sighed.

“Zhou Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“You’re lucky I love you.”

That got a smile out of him.

“Very lucky.”

She slipped the key into her pocket.

Then she looked at the balcony door.

“Do you think we should test it?”

“Test what?”

“The spare key.”

He looked at her.

“No.”

“Why?”

“Because I don’t want to spend another evening outside.”

Her mouth tipped up.

“You’re no fun.”

He stepped closer and took the key from her pocket, placing it on the small shelf just inside the balcony door.

“Here.”

She watched him.

“That’s a good place.”

“I know.”

He turned to close the door.

Xiaoran caught his sleeve.

“Wait.”

He held her gaze.

She leaned forward and kissed him.

When she pulled away, he was smiling.

“What was that for?”

“For saving me.”

“I didn’t save you. Fang Ze did.”

She thought about it.

“Then I’ll thank him next time.”

Yichen’s smile faded slightly.

“Let’s hope there isn’t a next time.”

She laughed.

He closed the balcony door carefully, from the inside.

chapters.desc: An ordinary Wednesday, a dark suit, and a dinner he planned because they keep eating between calls.
chapters.title: A Night Worth Dressing Up For
chapters.epigraph: “I wanted an evening where neither of us had to think about anything else.”
chapters.content:
Xiaoran knew something was happening when Yichen came home and didn’t immediately change into his usual comfortable clothes.

He had just returned from an afternoon meeting and training session. Usually, the first thing he did after entering their apartment was loosen his watch, put his phone down, and head for the shower.

Today, however, he walked straight into the bedroom.

Xiaoran was sitting on the bed with her laptop, editing a presentation. She looked up when he entered.

“You’re home.”

“Mm.”

He pressed a kiss to her temple.

Then he opened the wardrobe.

Xiaoran watched him take out a dark suit.

She blinked, then blinked again.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“What are you doing?”

He hung the suit carefully on the wardrobe door.

“Getting ready.”

“For what?”

“Dinner.”

She met his eyes.

“With whom?”

He turned around.

“With you.”

There was a brief silence.

Xiaoran slowly closed her laptop.

“Are we going somewhere?”

“Yes.”

“Where?”

“Somewhere nice.”

She eyed him.

“That’s not an answer.”

Yichen smiled.

“You’re right.”

He walked toward her, bent down, and placed a hand beside her on the mattress.

“It’s a surprise.”

Her eyes immediately brightened.

“A surprise?”

“Yes.”

“What kind of surprise?”

“Dinner.”

“Yichen!”

He laughed and kissed her cheek.

“Six thirty. Take your time getting ready.”

She caught his wrist before he could straighten up.

“Wait. What should I wear?”

“Something you feel beautiful in.”

She stared at him.

He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“That’s all the guidance you’re getting.”

And then he left the bedroom.

Xiaoran looked at the closed door, then at the suit, then back at the door.

She slowly reached for her phone.

There was only one reasonable thing to do.

She needed to investigate.

By five o’clock, the bedroom had become a small fashion crisis.

Three dresses were lying across the bed.

One was too casual. One was too elaborate.

One was beautiful, but she couldn’t decide whether it was appropriate for a surprise dinner.

Xiaoran stood in front of the mirror wearing a simple satin dress, looking at herself from different angles.

She liked it.

But was it too much?

She picked up her phone and took a picture, then deleted it.

She took another.

Deleted that one too.

Eventually, she walked out of the bedroom.

Yichen was standing in the living room, fastening his watch.

He had already changed.

A dark tailored suit, a crisp white shirt, and a discreet watch. His hair was neatly styled, and he had chosen a fragrance that was familiar to her: woody, elegant, and subtle.

He looked up.

His eyes settled on her.

He didn’t say anything.

Xiaoran became aware of the dress she was wearing.

“What?”

Yichen’s gaze moved over her once, unhurriedly.

“Nothing.”

“Why are you looking at me?”

“Because you’re beautiful.”

She looked away, her face warm.

He approached her.

The closer he came, the more she noticed how well he was dressed. It wasn’t unusual for Yichen to look handsome, but tonight he seemed put together.

He stopped in front of her and adjusted one of the straps on her shoulder.

“This one?”

She nodded.

He looked at her again, and took his time about it.

Then he smiled.

“You’re going to make it difficult for me to concentrate on dinner.”

Her cheeks warmed.

“You’re exaggerating.”

“Possibly.”

He offered his hand.

“Shall we?”

Xiaoran had expected him to order a car.

Instead, Yichen led her down to the private parking area.

She followed him to his car, the one she had once driven round the bottom level of this car park at twenty kilometers an hour.

He unlocked it.

Xiaoran looked at the car, then at him.

“This one?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because I feel like driving tonight.”

Her mouth tipped up.

“You’re taking me on a date in this car?”

“I’m taking you on a date. The car is just transportation.”

She laughed.

“That’s a very Zhou Yichen answer.”

He opened the passenger door for her.

Before getting in, she looked at him.

“Wait.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“What?”

She stepped closer and straightened his lapel.

“You look very handsome.”

His expression softened.

“Thank you.”

She patted his chest once, satisfied.

“Okay. Now you can drive.”

Yichen laughed and closed the door after she settled in.

Inside, the car was quiet and comfortable. The leather seats were cool against her skin, and the subtle scent of his car mixed with the fragrance he wore.

He started the engine.

Xiaoran buckled her seat belt and looked at him.

“Can I ask where we’re going?”

“You can ask.”

“Will you tell me?”

“No.”

She gasped.

He smiled as he pulled out of the parking space.

The restaurant was in one of the city’s most exclusive districts.

It occupied the upper floor of a beautiful building, with a private entrance, discreet staff, and a view of the city skyline.

When the car stopped at the entrance, Xiaoran looked out of the window.

Then she looked at Yichen.

“Wait.”

He unbuckled his seat belt.

“What?”

“Is this...?”

He got out before she could finish.

A moment later, her door opened.

Yichen offered his hand.

She took it, stepping out carefully.

The restaurant’s entrance was elegant without being overly extravagant. Warm lighting spilled through the glass doors, and the staff greeted Yichen with quiet familiarity.

Xiaoran glanced at him.

“You’ve been here before?”

“Once.”

“With whom?”

He met her eyes.

“The club’s sponsors’ dinner.”

“Ah.”

He rested his hand lightly against her lower back as they entered.

The host greeted him by name and led them through the restaurant.

Their table was positioned beside a large window, overlooking the illuminated city. It was private enough for conversation, but not so secluded that it felt formal or uncomfortable.

Xiaoran looked around.

The table was beautifully arranged, with delicate flowers, polished cutlery, and soft candlelight.

She sat down slowly.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“This is really nice.”

“I’m glad.”

She looked at the menu, then looked at the prices.

Her eyes widened slightly.

She quickly lowered it.

Yichen noticed.

He didn’t comment immediately.

Instead, he took his seat opposite her and unfolded his napkin.

“Do you like the view?”

She nodded.

“Very much.”

“Good.”

He picked up the menu.

“I thought you’d enjoy somewhere quieter tonight.”

Xiaoran looked at him.

“Why?”

He met her eyes.

“Because we’ve both been busy.”

She softened.

“That’s true.”

“Your deadlines have been piling up, and my schedule hasn’t been particularly flexible lately. We keep having dinner at home, eating between calls, or rushing because one of us has somewhere to be. I wanted an evening where neither of us had to think about anything else.”

Xiaoran looked at him.

Then she smiled.

“You planned all this just because you wanted to have dinner with me?”

“Is that insufficient?”

“No.”

She shook her head.

“It’s very sufficient.”

His lips curved.

“Then let’s enjoy it.”

The dinner was everything Xiaoran had expected from an elite restaurant and more.

The staff explained each course with quiet precision. The presentation was beautiful, but the food wasn’t merely decorative. Every dish had its own flavour and texture, and Yichen had chosen a tasting menu with a few additional dishes he thought she might enjoy.

Xiaoran was interested in the dessert.

She examined it from every angle before tasting it.

Yichen watched her.

“What?”

She took another photograph.

“Nothing. It’s pretty.”

“Do you want me to take a picture of you?”

She looked up.

She smiled and handed him her phone.

He took several pictures, adjusting the angle when she asked him to.

“Wait, the lighting is too dark.”

He moved the phone slightly.

“Like this?”

“Yes.”

“Look here.”

She smiled.

He took the picture, then another.

And another.

When he handed the phone back, she examined the photos.

“Oh.”

“Good?”

“Very good.”

She looked up at him.

“You’re surprisingly good at this.”

“I’ve had practice.”

“With whom?”

He gave her a look.

She laughed.

“Right. Me.”

He reached across the table and gently touched her fingers.

“Who else?”

She smiled and turned her attention back to the dessert.

Yichen watched her take the first bite.

Her expression changed immediately.

He raised an eyebrow.

“Good?”

She nodded enthusiastically.

“Very.”

He moved his own dessert slightly toward her.

“Try mine.”

She tasted it, then looked at him.

“Yours is better.”

“Then we’ll exchange.”

She looked at his plate.

“Really?”

“Yes.”

She pushed her dessert toward him.

He accepted it without complaint.

Xiaoran smiled.

“You’re very generous tonight.”

“Only tonight?”

She pretended to consider.

“Most nights.”

“That’s better.”

After the main course, the conversation became slower.

There was no need to hurry.

They talked about work, her latest project at Morrow Studio, and an upcoming away game that would take Yichen out of Shanghai for several days.

Xiaoran told him about a client who wanted the logo bigger in every frame, including the one where it was already on the side of a building.

Yichen listened, occasionally asking questions.

Then she asked about his training.

He told her about a tactical adjustment the coach had been discussing and how the team had been working on defensive transitions.

She listened carefully, even though some of the terminology still confused her.

At one point, she frowned.

“Wait. So if the opponent does that, you have to move there?”

“Not exactly.”

“Then where?”

He explained it again, using the edge of his napkin to sketch a rough court layout.

Xiaoran leaned forward.

“Oh.”

“Understand?”

“Mostly.”

“Mostly?”

“I understand the drawing. I don’t understand why everyone has to run so much.”

He laughed.

“That’s basketball.”

She shook her head.

“Your job is very tiring.”

“It can be.”

She turned to him.

“Are you happy?”

The question came naturally, without any particular reason.

Yichen looked at her, then nodded.

“Yes.”

“Good.”

He reached for his glass.

“And you?”

“Happy?”

“With work.”

She thought.

“Yes. Tired, sometimes. A little overwhelmed, sometimes. But I like what I’m doing.”

“Good.”

She tilted her head.

“You’re asking like a very serious interviewer.”

“I want to know.”

Her expression softened.

“I know.”

They looked at each other.

Then Xiaoran reached across the table and placed her hand over his.

“Thank you for tonight.”

Yichen turned his hand beneath hers, holding it.

“You’re welcome.”

After dinner, Yichen didn’t immediately take her home.

Instead, he suggested they walk along the terrace outside the restaurant.

The city was bright beneath them, with traffic moving like streams of light through the streets.

Xiaoran stood beside the railing, looking out.

Yichen came to stand behind her, his hands resting lightly at her waist.

She leaned back against him.

“It’s beautiful.”

“Mm.”

She turned her head slightly.

“Do you come here often?”

“Not really.”

“Why?”

“Never had much reason to.”

She held his gaze.

He smiled.

“Until tonight.”

She laughed.

“You’re being romantic.”

He lowered his head and kissed her temple.

She turned around in his arms.

His suit jacket was still perfectly arranged, although she could see that his tie had loosened slightly during dinner.

She reached up and adjusted it.

“You’re very handsome tonight.”

“You’ve mentioned that.”

“I know. I want to mention it again.”

His mouth curved.

“Then I’ll accept the compliment again.”

She laughed.

Then she looked at him more closely.

“Actually, you know what?”

“What?”

“I like seeing you dressed like this.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Why?”

“Because you usually come home in training clothes or comfortable clothes. Sometimes you look like you’ve just fought an entire basketball team.”

“I usually have.”

She laughed.

“But tonight, you look like... A very successful businessman.” She paused, searching for the right words.

That got a smile out of him.

“Is that a compliment?”

“Yes.”

“Then thank you.”

She tilted her head.

“But I like you in your basketball clothes, too.”

“I know.”

“And your ordinary clothes.”

“I know.”

“And when you’re wearing those ridiculous old T-shirts at home.”

He looked down at her.

“Ridiculous?”

“Some of them are.”

He laughed.

She smiled, then wrapped her arms around his waist.

“Basically, I like you in everything.”

Yichen’s expression softened.

He lowered his head and pressed a kiss into her hair.

“That’s fortunate.”

“Why?”

“Because I don’t plan on changing.”

The drive home was quieter.

Xiaoran sat comfortably in the passenger seat, one hand resting on the center console. Yichen drove with one hand on the steering wheel, the other occasionally reaching over to hold hers.

The city lights passed across his face.

She looked at him for a while.

Then said, “Can I tell you something?”

“Of course.”

“I was a little nervous when you told me to dress up.”

He glanced at her.

“Why?”

“I thought maybe we were going somewhere really formal. I wasn’t sure what to wear.”

“You looked beautiful.”

“I know. You told me.”

He smiled.

She said, “But I was also excited.”

“Good.”

“Because you planned everything.”

He squeezed her hand.

“I wanted to.”

She looked out of the window.

“Sometimes I feel like we spend so much time managing our schedules that we forget to have proper dates.”

Yichen was quiet.

Then he said, “We can make time.”

She turned toward him.

“Even with your training?”

“Even with training.”

“And my deadlines?”

“We’ll work around them.”

She couldn’t help smiling.

He said, “We don’t have to go somewhere expensive every time. But I don’t want us to get so comfortable that we stop making an effort.”

Xiaoran looked at him.

There was something about the way he said it that made her heart feel unusually full.

She squeezed his hand.

“I don’t think you could ever make me feel like you stopped making an effort.”

He turned to her.

“Good.”

She smiled.

“Although I wouldn’t mind another dinner like this.”

Yichen laughed.

“I thought you might say that.”

When they arrived home, Yichen parked the car and came around to open her door.

Xiaoran stepped out, then waited while he locked the car.

She reached for his hand as they walked toward the elevator.

Just before the doors closed, she turned toward him.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Next time, I’ll plan the date.”

He held her gaze.

“All right.”

“Properly.”

“I look forward to it.”

“And I’ll take you somewhere nice.”

He laughed under his breath.

“Sounds good.”

She nodded, satisfied.

Then added, “But you have to wear something handsome.”

He glanced down at his suit.

“Like this?”

“Maybe.”

“Maybe?”

She grinned.

“I’ll decide later.”

Yichen shook his head, amused.

When they reached their apartment, he helped her take off her coat and hung it up.

She removed her earrings and placed them on the dresser, then turned around to find him watching her.

“What?”

He approached her.

“Nothing.”

“You’re looking at me again.”

“I like looking at you.”

She went quiet.

Yichen brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“Did you have a good evening?”

“Very good.”

“Good.”

She hooked a hand behind his neck and kissed him.

Once, then again, a little longer.

When she pulled away, he was smiling.

“What’s that for?”

“For planning a date with me.”

“I thought that was what the date was for.”

She laughed.

He drew her closer and kissed her temple.

Then, with a faint smile, he said, “You don’t have to wait for a special occasion to ask me out, Xiaoran.”

“I know.”

“Or to dress up.”

“I know.”

“Or to spend an evening together.”

She looked up at him.

“I know.”

He kissed her cheek.

“But I like giving you reasons to look forward to something.”

Her arms tightened around his waist.

And for a while, neither of them moved.

What she would remember wasn’t the view. It was the way he had opened the passenger door.

The way he had watched her enjoy dessert.

The way he had listened to her talk about work.

And the way he had made an ordinary Wednesday feel like an occasion worth dressing up for.

She smiled against his chest.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Next Wednesday?”

He laughed.

“Already planning the next one?”

“Just checking your availability.”

He pressed his mouth to her hair.

“For you? I’ll make time.”

chapters.desc: A cleaning schedule on the kitchen whiteboard, a free Sunday, and two people who keep getting distracted.
chapters.title: A Very Unproductive Sunday
chapters.epigraph: “We have the rest of the week to clean. I’d rather spend today with you.”
chapters.content:
The plan was simple.

Clean the apartment in the morning.

Wash the bedsheets. Vacuum the floors. Wipe the kitchen counters. Organize the wardrobe. Refill the household supplies. Maybe rearrange the living room a little.

By six in the evening, the apartment would be spotless, and they would have the rest of Sunday to themselves.

At least, that was what Xiaoran had written on the small whiteboard in the kitchen.

SUNDAY PLAN
9:00 — Breakfast
9:30 — Laundry
10:00 — Bedroom
11:00 — Living room
12:00 — Lunch
13:00 — Kitchen
14:00 — Bathroom
15:00 — Organize wardrobe
16:00 — Rest

Yichen had looked at the list the previous night.

“You’re very ambitious.”

Xiaoran had been pleased with herself.

“We have a whole day.”

“Mm.”

“And we’re both free.”

“Yes.”

“So we should use it properly.”

He had looked at her before smiling.

“All right, Manager Lin.”

She had pointed her marker at him.

“Don’t think you can escape your responsibilities.”

He had laughed.

Now, well before ten on Sunday morning, Yichen was discovering that the plan had already encountered its first obstacle.

The obstacle was his girlfriend.

More specifically, his girlfriend was lying on the kitchen counter.

Not sitting on a chair.

Not standing beside the counter.

Actually lying on it, with her upper body stretched across the cool marble surface while she watched him prepare breakfast.

Yichen glanced over from the stove.

“Xiaoran.”

“Hm?”

“What are you doing?”

“Supervising.”

He met her eyes.

“From there?”

“It’s a good view.”

He turned back to the eggs.

“Of what?”

“You.”

His mouth curved.

“Very productive.”

“I know.”

She watched him for a few seconds, then reached out and tugged gently at the hem of his shirt.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Can you make mine a little softer?”

“Your eggs?”

“Yes.”

He turned off the stove, divided the eggs between two plates, and placed hers in front of her.

“Anything else?”

She looked at the plate, then at him.

“A kiss.”

He kissed her hair.

She frowned.

“That’s not what I meant.”

He smiled.

“Then you should be more specific.”

She lifted her face.

He understood immediately and kissed her properly, one hand resting against the counter beside her.

When he straightened, Xiaoran was smiling.

“Thank you.”

“You’re welcome.”

He returned to breakfast.

Xiaoran watched him for another moment.

Then she looked at the whiteboard visible from the kitchen.

9:30 — Laundry.

It was already 9:50.

She decided not to mention it.

By 10:25, they had managed to finish breakfast.

They had also managed to spend fifteen minutes discussing whether the little ceramic bowl Xiaoran had bought last week was suitable for holding fruit.

Yichen thought it was.

Xiaoran thought it might be too small.

They eventually agreed to put it on the dining table and see how it looked.

Then she wanted to take a photograph. Then Yichen appeared in the background of the photograph. Then she asked him to move.

Then she decided she liked the photograph better with him in it.

By the time they finished, the breakfast dishes were still on the table.

Yichen looked at the clock.

“Ten thirty.”

Xiaoran followed his gaze.

“Oh.”

“Should we start?”

“Yes.”

He picked up the plates.

She picked up the cups.

They carried everything to the kitchen.

Yichen washed while Xiaoran dried.

For a while, they worked efficiently.

Then Xiaoran noticed that the sleeve of his shirt had slipped down.

“Your sleeve.”

He glanced at it.

“What about it?”

“It’s wet.”

He rolled it up.

“Better?”

She nodded.

Then, because his forearm was right there, she reached out and touched it.

Yichen looked at her.

Something in his face eased.

“You’re distracting me.”

“I’m not doing anything.”

“You’re holding my arm.”

She looked down. She was.

She let go.

“Sorry.”

He rinsed the plate.

A moment later, she reached for his hand again.

He laughed.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“Do you want to finish the dishes or not?”

“Yes.”

“Then let me finish this one.”

She nodded obediently.

He placed the clean plate on the rack.

She immediately leaned over and kissed his cheek.

“Good job.”

He turned his head slightly.

“Is that my reward?”

That made her grin.

“Would you like another?”

“Yes.”

She kissed his other cheek.

Yichen looked at her.

Then he put the dishcloth down.

He held out his hand.

She barely had time to laugh before he drew her closer and kissed her.

It wasn’t a long kiss, but when they parted, Xiaoran was smiling so brightly that Yichen knew they had just lost another few minutes.

He glanced toward the sink.

There were still two cups.

He turned to her.

“You’re a terrible assistant.”

She gasped.

“I’m an excellent assistant!”

“Your performance says otherwise.”

She reached for the dishcloth.

“Fine. I’ll do it myself.”

He laughed and handed it to her.

At 11:15, they finally entered the bedroom.

Xiaoran stood at the foot of the bed, holding a fresh set of bedsheets.

“First, we need to change these.”

Yichen pulled the blanket away.

“All right.”

They stripped the bed together.

Yichen handled the fitted sheet while Xiaoran gathered the pillowcases.

It was going surprisingly well until she attempted to tuck one corner of the sheet under the mattress.

The elastic slipped.

She tried again.

It slipped again.

She frowned at it.

“Why is this so difficult?”

Yichen looked over.

“Which corner?”

“This one.”

He walked around the bed.

“Here.”

He crouched and pulled the fabric into place.

“Hold this.”

She held the edge.

He stretched the opposite side, and together they secured it.

“There.”

Xiaoran looked at the neatly fitted sheet.

“Good.”

Yichen straightened.

“Next?”

She looked at the pillows, then at the bed, then at him.

“Wait.”

“What?”

She climbed onto the mattress and sat in the middle.

Yichen watched her.

“Xiaoran.”

“Just a second.”

She patted the sheet.

“It’s clean.”

“Yes.”

“And soft.”

“Yes.”

She leaned backward, testing it.

Then she lay down.

Yichen stared.

She looked up at him.

She opened her arms.

He glanced at the pillowcases.

“We haven’t finished.”

“Just for a minute.”

He knew that expression.

It was the same one she used when she wanted something but intended to pretend it was a small request.

He climbed onto the bed and lay beside her.

Xiaoran immediately rolled toward him.

She tucked her head under his chin.

Yichen rested one arm around her waist.

For a little while, they lay there.

Then Xiaoran shifted.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Do you think we should change the pillows too?”

He looked at the pillows beside them.

“They’re fine.”

“What about the duvet?”

“Also fine.”

“Maybe we should wash the mattress protector.”

“We can.”

She nodded.

Then she closed her eyes.

Yichen looked down at her.

“Are you sleeping?”

“No.”

“Your eyes are closed.”

“I’m resting them.”

He laughed under his breath.

“Of course.”

A few minutes passed.

Then he felt her hand move against his chest.

“Yichen.”

“Yes?”

“Can I ask something?”

“Go ahead.”

“Do you think we’re very lazy?”

He looked at the ceiling.

“Not yet.”

She laughed into his shirt.

At noon, they were still in the bedroom.

The bedsheets had been changed.

The pillows had been replaced.

But neither of them had left the bed.

Yichen was lying on his back, one arm behind his head. Xiaoran was practically draped over him, scrolling through her phone.

She laughed.

He glanced down.

“What?”

“Look.”

She turned her phone toward him.

It was a short video of a couple attempting to clean their apartment, only to end up dancing with a mop.

Yichen watched until the end.

“Accurate.”

She gasped.

“Are you saying we’re like that?”

“We’ve been in this room for nearly an hour.”

“We changed the sheets!”

“An impressive achievement.”

She smacked his chest lightly.

“You’re supposed to support me.”

“I am.”

He looked at the phone again.

“Perhaps we should dance with the mop.”

She burst out laughing.

Then she put her phone down and rested her chin on his chest.

“Let’s get up.”

“All right.”

Neither moved.

She waited.

Yichen waited.

A few seconds later, she smiled.

“You’re not getting up.”

“Neither are you.”

“Because you’re holding me.”

He looked at his arm around her waist.

“Would you like me to let go?”

She considered it, then shook her head.

“No.”

“Then we’re staying.”

Their lunch was supposed to be simple.

There were leftovers in the refrigerator, and Yichen suggested reheating them.

Xiaoran agreed.

They made it to the kitchen at 12:40.

She opened the refrigerator while Yichen took out the containers.

“There’s still some chicken.”

“Mm.”

“And vegetables.”

“Yes.”

“And rice.”

“Good.”

She looked at the ingredients, then at him.

“Actually, I want something else.”

Yichen paused.

“What would you like?”

“Something crispy.”

He looked at the refrigerator.

“Like what?”

She thought.

“Potatoes.”

“We don’t have potatoes.”

“Then something else.”

He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“Very specific.”

She opened the snack drawer.

Yichen watched her retrieve a packet of seaweed crackers.

“That’s not lunch.”

“I know.”

She opened another drawer and found a packet of instant noodles.

He raised an eyebrow.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“We have proper food.”

“I know.”

“Then why are you eating snacks?”

She met his eyes.

“Because we’re having an unproductive Sunday.”

He laughed.

“Is that what we’re calling it?”

“Yes.”

He took the packet from her and placed it on the counter.

“How about I make something?”

Her expression brightened.

“Really?”

“Yes. But you’re helping.”

She nodded enthusiastically.

“Of course.”

Yichen made a quick lunch while Xiaoran prepared the vegetables.

Or rather, she prepared some of them.

The rest of the time, she stood beside him, occasionally stealing small pieces of food.

He caught her reaching for a piece of chicken.

“That’s hot.”

She withdrew her hand.

“I know.”

“Then wait.”

She turned to him.

“Can I have a kiss while I wait?”

He turned toward her.

“You’re very demanding today.”

She smiled.

He leaned down and kissed her.

Then he returned to the stove.

Xiaoran waited approximately thirty seconds before stealing another piece.

Yichen didn’t even turn around.

“Xiaoran.”

She froze.

“How did you know?”

“I can hear you.”

She laughed.

After lunch, they finally started cleaning the living room.

Yichen vacuumed.

Xiaoran wiped the coffee table.

They were doing quite well.

Until Xiaoran found the television remote under the sofa.

“Yichen!”

He turned off the vacuum.

“What?”

“Look what I found.”

He looked at the remote.

“Good.”

“It was missing yesterday.”

“Yes.”

She pressed a button.

The television turned on.

A drama appeared on the screen.

Xiaoran looked at it, then at Yichen.

He already knew.

“No.”

“I didn’t say anything.”

“You were about to.”

That made her grin.

“Just one episode.”

“We’re cleaning.”

“One episode while we rest.”

“We haven’t finished.”

She walked toward him, holding the remote behind her back.

“Please?”

He looked at her.

She widened her eyes.

He sighed.

“How long?”

“Forty minutes.”

“That’s an episode.”

“Exactly.”

He considered the vacuum cleaner, then the television.

Then her face.

“All right.”

She immediately smiled.

“You’re the best.”

He put the vacuum away.

“You’re taking advantage of me.”

She took his hand.

“Come on.”

One episode became two.

Two became an argument about whether the male lead was being unnecessarily stubborn.

Yichen thought he was.

Xiaoran thought he was misunderstood.

They paused the drama several times to discuss it.

At one point, Xiaoran became so invested that she sat upright, gesturing at the screen.

“Look! Look at his expression! He obviously wants to explain!”

Yichen looked at her.

“He’s had three opportunities.”

“But he didn’t know what to say!”

“He could start with the truth.”

“That’s easy for you to say.”

Something in his face eased.

“Would you prefer I lie to you?”

She turned toward him.

“Of course not.”

“Then?”

“Then don’t compare real life to drama.”

He laughed.

She leaned back against him.

“You’re too logical.”

“And you’re too forgiving.”

“That’s why we’re a good couple.”

He kissed the side of her head.

“Perhaps.”

When the second episode ended, Xiaoran stretched.

Yichen looked at the clock.

“Three thirty.”

She followed his gaze, then slowly turned toward him.

“...Oh.”

“Yes.”

She looked toward the living room.

The coffee table was clean.

The floor wasn’t vacuumed.

There was a laundry basket beside the sofa.

The kitchen still needed attention.

The wardrobe remained untouched.

She sighed.

“We’re terrible.”

Yichen glanced at her.

“We’ve accomplished several things.”

“Like what?”

“We changed the bedsheets.”

She nodded.

“Yes.”

“We made lunch.”

“Yes.”

“We found the remote.”

She laughed.

“That’s not cleaning.”

“It was a significant discovery.”

She leaned against his shoulder.

“You’re making excuses.”

“Would you prefer I tell you we’re behind schedule?”

She held his gaze.

“No.”

He kissed her temple.

“Then don’t worry.”

At four, they made snacks.

This was entirely Xiaoran’s idea.

She had decided that if they were going to be unproductive, they might as well be properly unproductive.

They made popcorn, cut some fruit, and prepared two small plates of biscuits.

Yichen handled the popcorn while Xiaoran arranged the fruit.

She was pleased with the result.

“Look.”

He glanced at the plate.

“Very nice.”

“I made it pretty.”

“I can see that.”

She placed a strawberry near the edge, then another.

Then she moved one because the arrangement looked uneven.

Yichen watched her.

“Are we eating this or photographing it?”

“Both.”

She took a picture.

Then she took another.

Then she asked him to move his hand because it was in the frame.

He moved it.

She took another photograph.

Finally, she looked satisfied.

“Done.”

Yichen picked up a strawberry.

She slapped his hand lightly.

“Wait!”

He held her gaze.

“What?”

“I haven’t taken one of you holding it.”

He sighed, but his mouth was smiling.

“All right.”

She held out a strawberry.

He took it between his fingers and looked toward the camera.

“Smile.”

He gave her a smile.

“More.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Xiaoran.”

“Please.”

He leaned toward the camera, holding the strawberry near his mouth.

She took the picture.

Then she looked at it.

Her eyes widened.

“Oh.”

“What?”

“You’re very handsome.”

He laughed.

“Thank you.”

She looked at the photograph again, then at him.

“Can I have another?”

He put the strawberry down.

He opened his arms.

She stepped closer.

He slipped one arm around her waist and kissed her cheek.

She laughed.

“That’s not the picture I asked for.”

“Then take it.”

She raised her phone.

But instead of taking the photograph, she turned her face and kissed him.

Yichen smiled against her lips.

“You’re terrible at photography.”

“Why?”

“Because you keep forgetting to take the picture.”

She laughed.

By early evening, they had accepted that the apartment wouldn’t be spotless.

The laundry had been washed and dried. The kitchen counters were clean.

The living room had been vacuumed, eventually.

But the wardrobe remained untouched, and the bathroom still needed cleaning.

Xiaoran stood in front of the whiteboard.

She held the marker.

Yichen stood behind her, his arms loosely around her waist.

She crossed out several items, then stared at the remaining list.

“Look at this.”

He rested his chin against her head.

“Mm.”

“We didn’t finish.”

“No.”

“At all.”

“We did some things.”

She looked at him.

“Are you not disappointed?”

He considered it.

“Not particularly.”

“Why?”

He turned her gently toward him.

“Because it’s Sunday.”

Her mouth tipped up.

“That’s your explanation?”

“Yes.”

He moved her hair off her cheek.

“We have the rest of the week to clean. I’d rather spend today with you.”

Her expression softened.

“You say that now, but tomorrow you’ll be looking for your missing socks.”

“I can survive.”

“And the bathroom?”

“Can wait.”

“The wardrobe?”

“Also.”

She smiled.

“You’re a bad influence.”

Yichen leaned down and kissed her.

“Am I?”

“Very.”

He kissed her again, a little longer this time.

When he pulled away, she was smiling.

“Maybe we should make a new plan.”

“What kind?”

She looked at the whiteboard, then at him.

“Next Sunday, we clean properly.”

“All right.”

“And no distractions.”

“Agreed.”

She gave him a suspicious look.

“You’re agreeing too easily.”

That got a smile out of him.

“Do you want me to disagree?”

She laughed.

“No.”

He kissed her.

“Then it’s settled.”

At night, Xiaoran was already in bed when Yichen finished locking the balcony door.

He turned off the bedroom lights, leaving only the bedside lamp on.

She was sitting against the headboard, wearing one of his shirts and holding her phone.

She reached for him.

Yichen climbed into bed.

She immediately moved toward him, settling against his side.

He pulled the blanket over them.

He kissed her temple.

She tilted her head.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Did you enjoy today?”

He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“Yes.”

She laughed.

“That’s terrible.”

He brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“We had breakfast together. We changed the sheets. We made lunch. We watched television. We made snacks.”

“And kissed.”

“Quite a lot.”

She grinned.

“That’s important.”

“Very.”

She rested her head against his chest.

For a while, neither spoke.

Then Xiaoran lifted her head.

“Wait.”

Yichen looked down.

“What?”

“We forgot the bathroom.”

He stared at her, then laughed.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“Go to sleep.”

“But—”

“We’ll clean it tomorrow.”

She considered that, then smiled.

“Okay.”

She settled against him again.

A few minutes passed.

Yichen thought she had fallen asleep when she spoke once more.

“Yichen?”

“Yes?”

“Next Sunday, let’s not make a schedule.”

He looked down at her.

“Why?”

“Because we never follow it.”

He laughed.

“That’s a reasonable conclusion.”

She smiled with her eyes closed.

“Maybe we should just do things slowly.”

He kissed her hair.

“That sounds better.”

She shifted closer, slipping one arm around his waist.

“And if we get distracted...”

“We get distracted.”

He smiled.

She laughed.

“Goodnight.”

“Goodnight, Xiaoran.”

Yichen glanced once at the whiteboard visible through the open bedroom door.

16:00 — Rest.

They had missed that schedule by several hours.

He smiled, turned off the bedside lamp, and pulled her a little closer.

chapters.desc: Her father still hasn’t quite said what he thinks of Yichen. Then there is a note under the rice cooker.
chapters.title: The Note Under the Rice Cooker
chapters.epigraph: “And he said I should look after you.”
chapters.content:
Yichen had been to Xiaoran’s family home enough times to know where everything was.

He knew which cupboard held the tea, which drawer contained the spare chopsticks, and which floorboard near the kitchen made a faint clicking sound when stepped on.

He also knew that Xiaoran’s mother would always ask whether he had eaten, regardless of whether he had arrived five minutes after lunch or five minutes before dinner.

What he hadn’t quite figured out was her father.

Not because her father was unfriendly. Quite the opposite. He was warm, easygoing, and had always treated Yichen kindly. They could talk about university, basketball, and occasionally the news. Sometimes her father even asked him to help with small things around the house.

But there was something about the older man that made Yichen careful.

Perhaps it was because Yichen genuinely respected him.
